title: 4 Keys Keyboard
statement:
A special keyboard has four keys:

- **A**: prints one letter `A` on the screen.
- **Ctrl-A**: selects everything currently on the screen.
- **Ctrl-C**: copies the current selection into the clipboard buffer. If nothing is selected it does nothing.
- **Ctrl-V**: appends the contents of the buffer to the end of the text already on the screen. The screen is not replaced and the buffer is not emptied, so you can paste the same buffer many times.

Pressing `A` or `Ctrl-V` clears the selection. The screen and the buffer both start empty.

You press keys exactly `N` times. Return the maximum number of `A` characters that can be on the screen at the end.
output_format: Print a single integer: the maximum number of `A` characters on the screen after `N` key presses.

examples.explanation: With only three presses there is no time to copy and paste profitably; press `A` three times.
Press `A`, `A`, `A` (3 letters), then `Ctrl-A`, `Ctrl-C`, `Ctrl-V`, `Ctrl-V`. The buffer holds 3 letters and is pasted twice, giving 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.
Reach 9 letters in 7 presses as above, then press `Ctrl-A`, `Ctrl-C`, `Ctrl-V`, `Ctrl-V`: the buffer holds 9 letters and is pasted twice, giving 27.

hints: Let `dp[i]` be the best screen length after `i` presses. One option is to just press `A` once more: `dp[i - 1] + 1`.
The other option is to end with a block that copies and then pastes: pick a point `j`, press Ctrl-A and Ctrl-C right after `j` presses, then spend the remaining presses on Ctrl-V.
That block uses 2 presses for select+copy and `i - j - 2` pastes, so the screen becomes `dp[j] * (i - j - 1)`. Take the maximum over all `j ≤ i - 3`.
